title: Tri-state phase-frequency detector with charge-pump (PLL loop-filter front end)
topology: A tri-state phase-frequency detector (PFD), built from two edge-triggered D flip-flops (reference and feedback clock as clocks, both D inputs tied high) with their Q outputs (UP and DOWN) fed back through an AND gate into a shared asynchronous reset, drives a charge pump: an UP pulse turns on a current source that sources charge onto the loop-filter capacitor, a DOWN pulse turns on a current sink that removes charge, and the reset immediately after both outputs go high (the AND-gate reset condition) creates a narrow simultaneous UP/DOWN pulse that eliminates the PFD's dead zone. Unlike a simple XOR phase detector, the tri-state PFD detects frequency error as well as phase error (its output has a consistent sign when the two clock frequencies differ, not just when they are out of phase), giving the loop an unbounded capture range independent of loop bandwidth.
spec_class: PHY-class PLL front end -- phase/frequency error-to-current converter driving the loop filter, used in essentially every charge-pump PLL (clock generation, clock-data recovery, frequency synthesis) regardless of the VCO topology downstream

pdk_portability.notes: The PFD's digital flip-flop/AND-gate logic is entirely standard-cell-portable (any digital PDK's flip-flop and AND-gate cells work, including sky130's sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell library); no re-derivation is needed beyond confirming setup/hold margins at the target clock frequency. The charge pump's current-source/current-sink transistors and switches are sky130-specific in their W/L sizing (mirror ratios, output-impedance/current-mismatch behavior depend on sky130's device models) and must be re-simulated for a new PDK, though the cascoded-current-source topology used to minimize charge-sharing/mismatch is fully portable.

sizing_approach: Size the charge-pump's up and down current sources to be closely matched (mirror-ratio matched, ideally cascoded to raise output impedance and suppress current mismatch across the loop-filter's voltage swing) since UP/DOWN current mismatch directly creates a periodic reference spur at the PFD comparison frequency; set the absolute charge-pump current together with the loop-filter resistor/capacitor values to hit the target loop bandwidth and phase margin from the standard second-order charge-pump-PLL transfer function; size the reset-path delay (the AND-gate-to-reset propagation delay) to produce a minimum simultaneous UP/DOWN pulse just wide enough to fully turn on both charge-pump switches and eliminate the dead zone, without wasting so much width that it needlessly raises the reference spur.
layout_idioms: matched, symmetric layout of the UP and DOWN charge-pump current-source/current-sink transistor pairs (common-centroid where area allows) to minimize the systematic current mismatch that creates reference spurs

cascode devices placed close to their current-source counterparts to minimize the parasitic capacitance that would otherwise slow charge-pump switching and widen the effective dead-zone-cancellation pulse
symmetric clock-tree routing of the reference and feedback clocks into the two PFD flip-flops so PFD-external skew does not masquerade as a static phase offset

the charge-pump output node routed short and direct to the loop-filter capacitor, with the switch transistors placed immediately adjacent to minimize charge injection and clock feedthrough onto the control voltage

source.citation: F. M. Gardner, "Charge-pump phase-lock loops," IEEE Transactions on Communications, vol. COM-28, no. 11, pp. 1849-1858, Nov. 1980.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its charge-pump PLL linearized loop analysis and the resulting loop-filter sizing methodology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is the foundational reference introducing the charge-pump PLL as an analysis framework; the tri-state PFD-plus-charge-pump front end described here is the near-universal implementation that realizes the current-output phase/frequency detector this analysis assumes.

notes: The dead-zone-elimination reset delay is the single most commonly under-sized parameter in first-pass PFD/charge-pump designs -- too short and the loop exhibits a dead zone (poor in-band phase noise / high jitter near lock), too long and the reference spur grows; always verify with a transient simulation sweeping input phase difference through zero, not just a linear small-signal loop model. This entry is the front-end companion to either VCO entry in this KB (cmos-ring-vco-current-starved or sky130-lc-vco-cross-coupled) -- the charge-pump's output drives the loop filter that in turn drives the VCO's control voltage.
